questions.q: Express $9.43\overline{87}$ in p/q form.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, options dekh kar base $9900$ confirm hai kyuki 2 digits pe bar hai aur 2 digits bin-bar point ke baad hain. Seedha subtraction laga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Pura number bina point ke likh aur usme se wo hissa ghata de jis par bar nahi hai. Khel khatam!

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Numerator} = 94387 - 943 = 93444 \\ \text{Fraction} = \frac{93444}{9900} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Standard textbook approach me $x$ ki equation banake subtract kiya jata hai decimals ko shift karne ke liye.

Mathematically :-

$$ x = 9.438787\dots \\ 10000x = 94387.8787\dots \\ 100x = 943.8787\dots \\ 9900x = 93444 \implies x = \frac{93444}{9900} $$

TCS Trap: Bacche non-repeating part $9$ subtract karna bhul jate hain jo decimal ke pehle hota hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Decimal trick: $ab.cd\overline{ef} = \frac{abcdef - abcd}{9900}$ seedha implement maar.

questions.q: Find the last two digits of the sequence $1234\dots$ up to exactly $138$ digits.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, counting series ka boundary wala khel hai. $1$ se $9$ tak $9$ digits ud gaye, baaki saare 2-digit number sequence banayenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Bache hue digits ko 2 se divide kar. Kitne pure numbers aaye aur kitna remainder bacha (jo aakhiri kata hua digit hoga) wo nikal le.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Remaining Digits} = 138 - 9 = 129 \\ \frac{129}{2} = 64 \text{ full numbers } + 1 \text{ extra digit} \\ \text{Last full number} = 9 + 64 = 73 \\ \text{Next number starts with } 7 \text{ (from } 74) \\ \text{Sequence ends:} \dots 72, 73, 7 \implies \text{Last two} = 37 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Series logic se hume exactly nikalna padta hai ki counting kahan tak pahuchegi. Arithmetic counting formula check karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ d(1 \dots N) = 9 + 2(N - 9) \text{ for 2-digit } N \\ 9 + 2(N - 9) = 137 \text{ (closest even match)} \\ 2(N - 9) = 128 \implies N = 73 \\ 138\text{th digit is first digit of } 74, \text{ which is } 7 $$

TCS Trap: Options me seedha $74$ baithega taki tum '1 extra digit' bhool kar pura 74 append karke tick mar do.

Exam Takeaway:

> Hamesha block break karo. $1-9$ = 9 digits. $10-99$ = 180 digits. Extra digit hamesha next number ki starting place nikalta hai.

questions.q: Find the remainder when the polynomial $x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 5$ is divided by $x - 2$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Remainder theorem ka sabse direct hit hai. Divider ko zero rakho aur pen chalane ki zaroorat hi mat feel hone do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Divisor ko equals to zero maan kar seedha polynomial me $x=2$ phek de. Jo aayega wahi Remainder hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ x - 2 = 0 \implies x = 2 \\ (2)^3 - 3(2)^2 + 4(2) - 5 \\ 8 - 12 + 8 - 5 = -1 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Remainder Theorem state karta hai ki polynomial $P(x)$ ko jab linear divisor $x-a$ se divide karein to Remainder $P(a)$ hota hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ P(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x - 5 \\ R = P(2) \\ R = 8 - 12 + 8 - 5 = -1 $$

TCS Trap: Algebraic long division lagane ka try karega to wahan basic plus-minus mistakes hone ke 100% chances hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Divisor polynomial agar $ax-b$ form ka hai, toh Remainder is strictly equal to $P(b/a)$.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $888\dots 888$ (written 25 times) is divided by $37$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, same digit repeatedly aaye, aur divisor 37 ho, matlb 3-digit cyclicity wala rule direct udta hua aayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Ek digit agar $3$ baar repeat ho to wo $37$ se pura divide hota hai. Total 25 hai. $25$ ko $3$ se divide kar, remainder 1 digit bachega. Wahi aakhiri digit tumhara answer hoga.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Blocks of 3} = \frac{25}{3} \implies \text{Quotient } 8, \text{ Remainder } 1 \\ \text{One digit left} = 8 \\ 8 \pmod{37} = 8 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): repeating blocks $111$ divisibility logic. $111$ khud $37$ ka multiple hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ 888 = 8 \times 111 = 8 \times (3 \times 37) \text{ (Divisible)} \\ \text{24 digits will form } 8 \text{ such divisible blocks.} \\ \text{Final 25th digit is just } 8 \text{ itself.} $$

TCS Trap: Pattern figure out na karne pe kuch log isko basic expansion me convert karne baithenge jiska koi ant hi nahi hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Any single digit repeated 3 times ($aaa$) is unconditionally divisible by $3, 37, \text{ and } 111$.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $100!$ is divided by $101$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Denominator exactly $101$ prime hai aur factorial seedha ek kam yani $100!$ hai. Wilson Uncle zindabad!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Wilson Theorem lagao seedha. $(P-1)!$ ko kisi prime $P$ se divide kare to Remainder humesha $P-1$ hi hota hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ P = 101 \text{ (Prime)} \\ (101-1)! \pmod{101} \equiv -1 \pmod{101} \\ -1 + 101 = 100 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Standard theorem properties prove karke dikhati hai ki prime denominators saare middle terms ka pair inverses generate kar lete hain.

Mathematically :-

$$ (p-1)! \equiv p-1 \pmod p \\ 100! \equiv 101-1 \pmod{101} \equiv 100 $$

TCS Trap: Log Euler Totient thukne lagte hain yaha joki powers pe lagta hai, factorials pe bilkul fail hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Wilson's Theorem is a fixed cheat code: $(P-1)! / P$ always yields a remainder of $(P-1)$ if $P$ is prime.

questions.q: How many numbers between $400$ and $600$ begin with or end with the digit $5$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: "Between" ka word boundary lagata hai, 500s ki saari sequence start with $5$ ki bucket me aayegi. Union rule overlap minus karega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): $500$ se $599$ tak total $100$ numbers seedha mil gaye. Phir $401$ se $499$ me ending with $5$ wale total $10$ numbers milenge. Dono jod de.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Start with 5 } (500 \to 599) = 100 \text{ numbers} \\ \text{End with 5 in 400s } (405, 415 \dots 495) = 10 \text{ numbers} \\ \text{Total} = 100 + 10 = 110 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Formal set logic (inclusion-exclusion) use karo jisse overlapping sets theek se resolve hote hain.

Mathematically :-

$$ n(A) = 100 \text{ (starts with 5)} \\ n(B) = 20 \text{ (ends with 5 from } 401 \to 599) \\ n(A \cap B) = 10 \text{ (starts and ends with 5: } 505, 515\dots) \\ n(A \cup B) = 100 + 20 - 10 = 110 $$

TCS Trap: Baccha $505$ wale pure $10$ numbers ko start me bhi ginta hai aur end me bhi. Double count se $+10$ hoke options set hote hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Jab "Or" statement ho to Set theory intersection $n(A \cap B)$ minus karna kabhi mat bhulna.

questions.q: The total number of integers between $200$ and $400$, each of which either begins with $3$ or ends with $3$ or both, is
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: Bhai ekdum pichle type ki xerox copy hai sawal. Same frame, same counting base, same answer form.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): $300$ wali puri line uthao ($100$ numbers). Fir bach gaya $200$ series, usme har 10 digit me ek baar last me $3$ aata hai. Total 10 nikal ke jod.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Starts with 3: } 300 \dots 399 \implies 100 \\ \text{Ends with 3 in 200s: } 203, 213 \dots 293 \implies 10 \\ \text{Sum} = 100 + 10 = 110 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Wahi venn diagram lagti hai yaha, 3 start, 3 end and common numbers in 300s series.

Mathematically :-

$$ n(S_3) = 100, n(E_3) = 20 \\ n(S_3 \cap E_3) = 10 \text{ (like 303, 313...)} \\ \text{Total} = 100 + 20 - 10 = 110 $$

TCS Trap: Statement me likha "or both" padh ke log confuse hoke $110$ me phirse intersection wale $10$ add karke $120$ mark marte hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Union function "or both" ki condition apne formula block $n(A \cup B)$ me automatic handle karta hai, alag se add nahi karte.

questions.q: $M$, is the largest 4-digit number, which when divided by $4, 5, 6$ and $7$ leaves remainder as $2, 3, 4$ and $5$, respectively. What is the remainder when $M$ is divided by $9$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, Divisor aur Remainder ke beech difference dekh (4-2=2, 5-3=2). Jab gap same ho to us gap ko LCM ki complete value se negative offset maante hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Divisors ka LCM nikalo, largest 4-digit number uske pass tak le jao. Phir wo constant offset (-2) minus karo. Aur last me Digital sum se rule of 9 lagao.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{LCM}(4,5,6,7) = 420 \\ \frac{9999}{420} \implies Q=23, \text{ base val } = 9660 \\ \text{Target } M = 9660 - 2 = 9658 \\ 9658 \pmod 9 \implies 9+6+5+8 = 28 \implies 1 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): The equation template for such problems is $N = \text{LCM} \times k - (\text{Divisor} - \text{Remainder})$.

Mathematically :-

$$ M = 420k - 2 \\ 420 \times 23 - 2 = 9660 - 2 = 9658 \\ \frac{9658}{9} = 1073 \text{ with } R = 1 $$

TCS Trap: Students us constant gap $2$ ko minus karne ki jagah subtract karke check karte hain ki galti se plus toh nahi karna. Constant diff = Minus it.

Exam Takeaway:

> Jab saare $D_i - R_i = k$ same aayein, toh pattern humesha $\text{LCM}(D_1,D_2\dots) \times m - k$ banta hai.

questions.q: Find the last two digits of $3^{1000} \times 7^{1000}$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Jab exponents same ho, bases multiply kar. Jaise hi base end in $1$ (matlab 21) aayega, wahi puraani 'X1' wali jugad fix kar de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Combine the bases directly. Base 21 mil gaya. Tens place ke liye base tens ko power unit se multiply, and unit is obviously 1.

Mathematically :-

$$ (3 \times 7)^{1000} = 21^{1000} \\ \text{Unit digit} = 1 \\ \text{Tens digit} = (2 \times 0) \pmod{10} = 0 \\ \text{Result} = 01 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Using binomial expansion of form $(10x + 1)^n$, which expands to end with $(nx \pmod{10})1$.

Mathematically :-

$$ (20+1)^{1000} = \dots + {1000 \choose 1}(20)^1(1)^{999} + 1 \\ 20000 + 1 \implies \text{Last two are } 01 $$

TCS Trap: $3$ ka cyclicity alag, aur $7$ ka cyclicity alag nikalne beth jaoge toh multiplication me last two digits bura fasa dengi.

Exam Takeaway:

> Exponent rules apply first: $a^n \times b^n = (ab)^n$. Fir $(\dots X1)^Y$ wali solid tens trick apply karo.

questions.q: If the 9-digit number $7x79251y8$ is divisible by $36$, what is the value of $(10x^2-3y^2)$ for the largest possible value of $y$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisible by $36$ gives you $4$ and $9$. Keyword "largest possible value of $y$" bolke options restrict kar diye hain. Reverse top down scan lagana hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Last two digits $y8$ divisibility of 4 test me daal. Highest value 8 aayega. Uske baad bache digits ko digital sum rule 9 se balance karke $x$ nikal le.

Mathematically :-

$$ y8 \pmod 4 = 0 \implies y \in \{0, 2, 4, 6, 8\} \\ y_{max} = 8 \text{ (checks out as } 88 \text{ is div by 4)} \\ \text{Digital Sum: } 7+x+7+9+2+5+1+8+8 = 47+x \\ 47+x \pmod 9 = 0 \implies x=7 \text{ (since } 54 \text{ is mul)} \\ 10(7^2) - 3(8^2) = 490 - 192 = 298 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Always resolve the variable at the unit/tens end first, then resolve the summation variable using C9 restriction.

Mathematically :-

$$ y=8 \implies N = 7x7925188 \\ \text{Rule 9 requires } (47+x) = 9k \implies x=7 \\ \text{Ans: } 10(49) - 3(64) = 298 $$

TCS Trap: Jaldbazi me largest nahi pada to $y=0$ substitute kar loge pehle condition me. Calculation badhegi aur answer wrong ho jayega.

Exam Takeaway:

> Variables set karte time "Largest" ya "Smallest" wale conditions hamesha scan process uper ya niche se initiate karvate hain.

questions.q: Find the smallest Six digit number which is a perfect Square?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Ek perfect bound limits wala number hai. $100000$ base hai jiska root nikalna asaan hai, $316$ ke thik thoda aage girega. Matlb seedha $317$ ka square required answer hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): $317$ ka square nikalne ki Base 300 trick maar. Number me difference jod kar 3 se multiply, then difference ka square piche rakh.

Mathematically :-

$$ \sqrt{100000} \approx 316.22 \\ \text{Root needed is } 317 \\ 317^2 \to \text{Base } 300, \text{ offset } +17 \\ 3 \times (317 + 17) \mid 17^2 = 3 \times 334 \mid 289 \\ 1002 \mid 289 = 100489 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Long division approach se extra diff extract kiya ja sakta hai smaller squares me.

Mathematically :-

$$ 316^2 = 99856 \text{ (Largest 5-digit square)} \\ 317^2 = 100489 \text{ (Smallest 6-digit square)} $$

TCS Trap: Long division root pe 100000 daalke solve karte hue calculation blunder hona fix hai. Limits direct verify karo.

Exam Takeaway:

> Hamesha Base Boundaries ke absolute fix squares memorize karke ja: $316^2 = 99856$ (Max 5D) aur $317^2 = 100489$ (Min 6D).

questions.q: Find the total number of digits of $2^{24} \times 5^{12}$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Jaha base me $2$ aur $5$ dikh gaye ek sath, matlab zeroes wali machine mil gayi. Total zeroes ek limit par power ko 10 ki form me bhej dete hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): 2 aur 5 ki equal powers separate kar. Unko $10^n$ me tod. Baaki jo odd elements bache unka actual output evaluate kar, kitne digit honge aur usme utne zero laga de.

Mathematically :-

$$ 2^{24} \times 5^{12} = 2^{12} \times (2^{12} \times 5^{12}) \\ = 4096 \times 10^{12} \\ \text{Digits in } 4096 = 4 \text{ digits.} \\ \text{Total} = 4 + 12 = 16 \text{ digits.} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Using basic logarithm principles to compute characteristic of large scientific numbers. Char + 1 = total digits.

Mathematically :-

$$ \log_{10}(2^{24} \cdot 5^{12}) = 24 \log 2 + 12 \log 5 \\ 24(0.301) + 12(0.699) = 7.224 + 8.388 = 15.612 \\ \text{Digits} = \lfloor 15.612 \rfloor + 1 = 16 $$

TCS Trap: Logarithms pe jaoge toh multiplication decimal truncation ki values error karwa sakti hain, directly combine karo base 10 ko.

Exam Takeaway:

> Jab $2$ and $5$ exist uniformly, hamesha smaller power ko completely pack karke multiples of $10$ eliminate karo.

questions.q: A 6-digit number $524x8y$ is divisible by $36$. What is the maximum possible value of $(x + y)$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai $36$ matlb phirse $4$ and $9$. Aur is baar individual maximums hit karne bol raha hai kyunki aggregate result maxima me chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Sum of $(x+y)$ max karna hai toh individual bounds max kar. Last 2 se $y=8$ confirm. Phir digital rule of 9 se limit set kar jisme $x$ check ho max tak.

Mathematically :-

$$ y \in \{0, 4, 8\} \implies y_{max} = 8 \text{ (Div by 4)} \\ \text{Digital Sum} = 5+2+4+x+8+8 = 27+x \\ (27+x) \pmod 9 = 0 \implies x \in \{0, 9\} \\ x_{max} = 9 \\ x+y = 9+8 = 17 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): If multiple possibilities arise, take the absolute bounding box. Sub in largest parameters possible.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{For } y=8 \implies x=0 \text{ or } 9 \implies (0+8=8, \text{ or } 9+8=17) \\ \text{For } y=4 \implies x=4 \implies (4+4=8) \\ \text{Max is absolutely } 17 $$

TCS Trap: C9 test karte time agar base number $27$ nikal aaye toh mostly bacche next parameter ignore karke seedha $x=0$ man lete hain, maximum check zero pe miss ho jata hai

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $[7^{(4n+3)}] \times 6^n$, where $n$ is a positive integer?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Variables power me hain. Kisi variable value formula limit se answer change nahi hone wala toh seedha apna manchaha independent constant rakh de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Variable dekh ke confuse mat hona. Seedha $n=1$ dal equation me aur constants nikal. 6 ki koi power wese bhi 6 rehti hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Put } n = 1 \\ 7^{4(1)+3} \times 6^1 = 7^7 \times 6 \\ 7^7 \equiv 7^3 = 343 \implies \text{Unit is } 3 \\ 3 \times 6 = 18 \implies \text{Result ends in } 8 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Core cyclic repetition rule follow karke formula break kiya ja sakta hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ 7^{4n+3} = (7^4)^n \times 7^3 \\ 1^n \times 343 \implies \text{Unit 3} \\ 6^n \equiv 6 \\ \text{Final} = 3 \times 6 = 18 \implies 8 $$

TCS Trap: Algebraic variable powers dekh kar hi bacche approach drop kar dete hain assumption nikaalne wali galti ke darr se.

Exam Takeaway:

> Algebraic variables in exponent expressions sirf dikhave ke hote hain, put simplest basic values like $1$ or $2$ to crack unit digit instantly.

questions.q: From $500$ to $750$ (including both) how many natural numbers are there are which are neither Divisible by $3$ or $11$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: Range me set theory direct apply karni hai. Multiplication limits exact hit karke numbers formulate karo union nikalne ke liye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Exact bracket multiples trick lagao upper minus lower floor range me. Dono sets aur overlap (33) ka counting nikal, total numbers subtract maar union value.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Total} = 750 - 500 + 1 = 251 \\ n(3) = \lfloor750/3\rfloor - \lfloor499/3\rfloor = 250 - 166 = 84 \\ n(11) = \lfloor750/11\rfloor - \lfloor499/11\rfloor = 68 - 45 = 23 \\ n(33) = \lfloor750/33\rfloor - \lfloor499/33\rfloor = 22 - 15 = 7 \\ \text{Neither} = 251 - (84 + 23 - 7) = 151 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): This translates exactly to De Morgan's Law mapping for discrete bounds limits.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Neither} = n(U) - n(A \cup B) \\ = 251 - (n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)) \\ = 251 - 100 = 151 $$

TCS Trap: Range $500$ "including both" skip karke log direct total $750-500 = 250$ le kar minus $1$ ka error la denge.

Exam Takeaway:

> Exact interval range of multiples finding trick: $\lfloor b/k \rfloor - \lfloor (a-1)/k \rfloor$.

questions.q: When a number is divided by $65$, the remainder is $31$. When the same number is divided by $13$, the remainder is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Pehla divisor $65$, exactly dusre divisor $13$ ka multiple $(13 \times 5)$ hai. Seedha purane remainder pe strike maar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Jo pura remainder hai (31) usi ko naya divisor (13) maanke seedha operation complete kar de.

Mathematically :-

$$ 65 \pmod{13} == 0 \text{ (Condition passed)} \\ 31 \pmod{13} \implies 31 - (13 \times 2) = 31 - 26 = 5 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): By Division Lemma algorithm, $N = 65k + 31$. Extract $13$ completely.

Mathematically :-

$$ N = 13(5k) + 13(2) + 5 \\ N = 13(5k+2) + 5 \implies \text{Remainder is } 5 $$

TCS Trap: TCS pehla divisor multiple nahi rakhega (like $D_1=65$, $D_2=14$), us case me operation invalid hota hai answer "Cannot be determined" ayega.

Exam Takeaway:

> Rule constraint: Agar pehla divisor dusre se perfect divide hota hai to final Remainder sidha $R_1 \pmod{D_2}$ hota hai.

questions.q: In a farm, there are some cows and some hens. If heads are counted, there are $180$. If legs are counted, there are $420$. How many cows are there in the farm?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Triplet Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Farm/Zoo and Wheel problems purely Junior Satisfaction Method (JSM) se hi hit kiye jate hain. Base assumption hen se shuru hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Maan le saare 180 janwar Murgiyan hain. Matlab minimum 2 pair hone chaiye sabke, 360 expected pair. Jo difference aya usko bache hue extra legs 2 per cow me baant de.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Assume 100\% Hens (2 legs): } 180 \times 2 = 360 \text{ legs.} \\ \text{Extra Legs} = 420 - 360 = 60 \\ \text{Cows count} = \frac{\text{Extra Legs}}{4 - 2} = \frac{60}{2} = 30 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Classical approach substitution of variables pe chalta hai, jo time leta hai exam me.

Mathematically :-

$$ H + C = 180 \implies H = 180 - C \\ 2H + 4C = 420 \\ 2(180-C) + 4C = 420 \\ 360 + 2C = 420 \implies 2C = 60 \implies C = 30 $$

TCS Trap: $X$ aur $Y$ linear equation banwa kar tumhara calculation error badhane ki koshish chalegi average students par.

Exam Takeaway:

> JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) is the absolute fastest hack to eliminate linear equation setups for Head/Leg constraints.

questions.q: How many numbers are there between $99$ and $1000$ such that the digit $8$, occupies the unit's place?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: Range 99-1000 exactly 3-digit array define karti hai. Positions fix karke directly possibilities multiplier maar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Teen box bana digits ke liye. Last me sirf ek possibility ($8$) fix. First digit 0 nahi ho sakti (1 se 9). Second (middle) digit pe koi rok nai ($0$ se $9$). Multiply maar de.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Box } [H][T][U] \\ \text{Places count} \implies (9 \text{ opts}) \times (10 \text{ opts}) \times (1 \text{ opt fix } 8) \\ = 9 \times 10 \times 1 = 90 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Arithmetic progression bana ke total terms formuli se mapping karte hain basic level pe.

Mathematically :-

$$ AP = 108, 118, 128 \dots 998 \\ L = a + (n-1)d \\ 998 = 108 + (n-1)10 \\ 890 = 10(n-1) \implies n = 90 $$

TCS Trap: Arithmetic approach me log limits lene (first term) me phaste hain. Permutation places concept limits eliminate kar deta hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Digits placement constraints wale array count questions mostly Permutations (places fix multi) se solve hone chahiye AP series se nahi.

questions.q: For the number $7200$, find the number of factors divisible by $40$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Jis condition pe fix karna hai number ko wo us factor base ka core multiplier block ban jayega. Us core block ko pura expression se nikal do bahar.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): 7200 ko fully factorize kar. Aur divisor 40 ko bracket common me bahar khich le. Ab andar kitni terms fraction factors bach gaye, bas unpe factor power formula maar.

Mathematically :-

$$ 7200 = 72 \times 100 = 2^5 \times 3^2 \times 5^2 \\ \text{Constraint Divisor } = 40 = 2^3 \times 5^1 \\ \text{Take } 40 \text{ out: } 2^3 \times 5^1 (2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5^1) \\ \text{Total terms inside} = (2+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 3 \times 3 \times 2 = 18 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Direct probability permutation limit. Set up boundary thresholds needed for exponent ranges.

Mathematically :-

$$ N = 2^a \cdot 3^b \cdot 5^c \text{ (multiple of } 2^3 \cdot 5^1) \\ a \in \{3,4,5\} (3), \, b \in \{0,1,2\} (3), \, c \in \{1,2\} (2) \\ 3 \times 3 \times 2 = 18 $$

TCS Trap: Total divisor factor nikalte ho sab aur bad me divide karke options check karte ho jo pura waste of time block banega.

Exam Takeaway:

> Restricted multiple divisor nikalte time absolute divisor requirement bahar nikalkar bachi powers factor formula count me lo.

questions.q: The average of $1088$ real numbers is zero. At most, how many of them can be negative?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Zero-sum restriction matrix dikh rahi hai. Bada positive ek side, baaki negatives samne rakh ke value shift symmetry laga do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Sum zero lane ke liye ek bohot bada positive number lakar baaki ke $N-1$ negative numbers ka wazan completely sambhala ja sakta hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Assume } 1087 \text{ numbers are } -1 \\ \text{To make sum } 0, \text{ the } 1088\text{th number must be } +1087 \\ \text{Max negatives allowed} = 1087 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute proof formula that zero-sum equation handles bounds constraint limits.

Mathematically :-

$$ \sum_{i=1}^{N} x_i = 0 \\ x_1 + x_2 \dots x_{N-1} = -x_N \\ \text{Max elements for arbitrary } -x_N \text{ is } N - 1 $$

TCS Trap: Yahan $50\%$ symmetry lagti hai logical traps me aur baccha galat $544$ tick kar deta hai sum ko equate karne ki theory follow karke.

Exam Takeaway:

> Zero-sum operations me individual elements pe extreme property puche, toh $N-1$ absolute maximum limit hoti hai.

questions.q: The $55x41y$ is a six-digit even number and is completely divisible by $33$, then among the following $(x^2 + y^2)$ is divisible by: ($x$ and $y$ are non-zero)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Even aur divisibility dono variables fasa rhi hai. Piche $y$ constraint sirf even lega $0$ neglect karke (non-zero). Phir substitution linear equations lagani hogi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Last digit even hai, non zero. Substitue $y \in \{2,4,6,8\}$. $11$ ka divisibility format setup karke single bound output pick karo jo $3$ ka rule set follow kare.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{11 diff: } (5+x+1) - (5+4+y) = x-y-3 = 0 \text{ or } 11 \\ x-y = 3 \implies x = y+3 \\ \text{3 Sum: } 15+x+y = \text{multi 3} \implies x+y = 3k \\ \text{Put } y=6 \implies x=9. \text{ (Sum } x+y=15 \text{ passed rule of 3)} \\ 9^2 + 6^2 = 81 + 36 = 117 = 13 \times 9 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Full scale equation elimination process in variables limits constraints.

Mathematically :-

$$ x - y \equiv 3 \pmod{11} \text{ (Since diff limit checks)} \\ x + y \equiv 0 \pmod 3 \\ \text{Try } y=2 \to x=5 (5+2=7 \text{ not } /3) \\ \text{Try } y=4 \to x=7 (7+4=11 \text{ not } /3) \\ \text{Try } y=6 \to x=9 (15 \pmod 3=0) \\ 81 + 36 = 117 $$

TCS Trap: Students word "Even Number" ignore kar dete hain initial me ya phr non zero nahi padhte aur $y=0$ pe attempt shuru kar dete hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Overlapping parameters given hon to filter limit (Even / Non Zero) ko core variable base assume kiya karo calculation filter karke.

questions.q: What is the largest 4-digit number that is exactly divisible by $88$?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: Largest condition and $88$ divisibility criteria (yani rule 11 aur 8 check). Top se sabse bada number scan kar option list me.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Options largest to smallest line lagao. Pehle 8 aur 11 ka rule check kar direct reject condition udate ja.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Largest } 9988 \implies \frac{988}{8} \text{ fails} \\ 9966 \implies \frac{966}{8} \text{ fails} \\ 9944 \implies \frac{944}{8} = 118. \text{ And } 11 \text{ checks } (13 - 13 = 0). \\ \text{Answer fixed } = 9944 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Arithmetic absolute LCM remainder limit test apply karna traditional way me.

Mathematically :-

$$ \frac{9999}{88} \implies \text{Quotient } 113, \text{ Remainder } 55 \\ 9999 - 55 = 9944 $$

TCS Trap: Traditional minus karoge toh Remainder me galati aana boht aam hai and $9900$ wagera match limit set hote hain errors me.

Exam Takeaway:

> Jab "Largest/Smallest Divisible Array Number" question complete options ke sath ho, Reverse Top Down test options ka 10x fast execution hai.

questions.q: Find the rightmost two non-zero digits of $30^{2720}$.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Value Putting & Symmetry.

Pen-Free Observation: Trailing zeroes kisi number form me extra multiple limits add karti hain. Pura Zero block hi ignore maro matrix separation property lagake.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Zero nikal bahar kar de 10 multiple split lagake. Baaki sirf $3$ bachega base. 3 ke upar power exact $4$ ki multiplier sequence me fit baith rhi hai matlab 81 banayegi series ko 'X1' solve ke lie.

Mathematically :-

$$ 30^{2720} = (3 \times 10)^{2720} = 3^{2720} \times 10^{2720} \\ \text{Ignore zeroes part} \to 3^{2720} \\ 3^{2720} = (3^4)^{680} = 81^{680} \\ \text{Unit} = 1 \text{, Tens} = (8 \times 0) = 0 \implies 01 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Exact cyclical behavior and modular inverse scaling on core number parts.

Mathematically :-

$$ \phi(100) = 40 \\ 3^{40k} \equiv 1 \pmod{100} \\ 2720 \pmod{40} = 0 \implies \text{Last two are } 01 $$

TCS Trap: Yahan decimal zeros aur extra zeros add hone ki confusion lagakar numbers $10^{X}$ ko directly mix karke powers calculate karne mat baitho.

Exam Takeaway:

> Trailing zeroes check limits me core non zero base separate mark karo, aur remaining portion power cyclicity rules execute karo.

questions.q: The difference between a two-digit number and the number obtained by interchanging the positions of its digits is $54$. The difference between the two digits of that number is?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Reversed positions wale difference condition hamesha $9$ ka perfectly clean multiple extract deta hai variable format ke liye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Interchanging digits ka difference diya ho to seedha given number (54) ko 9 se divide kar do, limits aur answer clear output degi.

Mathematically :-

$$ (10x + y) - (10y + x) = 9(x - y) \\ 9(x - y) = 54 \implies (x - y) = 6 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Full linear algebraic setup variable extraction based on placeholders formulation.

Mathematically :-

$$ N = 10a + b \text{ , Reverse } R = 10b + a \\ N - R = 9a - 9b = 9(a-b) \\ 9(a-b) = 54 \implies a-b=6 $$

TCS Trap: Students actual two-digit combinations nikalne ko assume karte hain like 93-39 jo ki manual hit-and-trial pe bhot heavy limit waste karta hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> Interchanged Reverse Difference is directly $9(x-y)$. And Reversed Addition Sum is perfectly $11(x+y)$ always.

questions.q: Find the number of factors of $46656$ (which is $2^6 \times 3^6$) that are BOTH a perfect square and a perfect cube.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Ek factor jo power 2 (Square) aur power 3 (Cube) dono ka perfectly balance divisor hai, uske andar LCM power 6 perfectly align hona chahiye base matrix pe.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Hamesha square aur cube limits ko eliminate karo unka LCM bana ke yani 6 multiplier factor search karke. Total possible $6$ multiple limit ko pick karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Matrix Needed} = (P_1)^{6x} \times (P_2)^{6y} \dots \\ \text{Base factors } = 2^6 \times 3^6 \\ 6\text{th power possible for } 2 = \{2^0, 2^6\} \implies 2 \text{ choices} \\ 6\text{th power possible for } 3 = \{3^0, 3^6\} \implies 2 \text{ choices} \\ \text{Total Combos} = 2 \times 2 = 4 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Combinatorics check parameters filtering exactly out non overlapping boundaries limits.

Mathematically :-

$$ x^a \text{ must have } a \pmod 2=0, a \pmod 3=0 \implies a \pmod 6=0 \\ \text{Since max power is 6, valid } a \in \{0,6\} \\ \text{Choices count} = 2 \times 2 = 4 $$

TCS Trap: Log common dhundhte hain dono ko (squares all nikalenge fir cubes ki alag process form kareinge) joki pura overlap checking waste operation hai.

Exam Takeaway:

> BOTH perfect Square and Perfect Cube operation ka universal standard matlab absolute factor matching $6\text{th}$ Base Power multiples limits.
